name: Findability: tool content in search surface (recall@10)

description: Baseline timeout: embedding 500 convs (2289 chunks) takes ~16min. Need to reduce scope or cache DB.
Baseline: exchange-window chunker, 50 convs, no tool content. recall@10=0.1951, hit@10=1.0 (semantic text already finds some tool-usage patterns)
Tool summaries: one chunk/conv with tool names, file paths, shell commands. recall@10: 0.1951→0.2812 (+44%). Big wins on shell.execute, git, grep queries.

Model comparison on 816-conv targeted micro-index (128-tok chunks): gte-base=0.887 (+10.7%), arctic-s=0.868 (+8.4%), arctic-m=0.847, bge-small=0.801, bge-base=0.773. gte-base clear winner. Micro-index scores, full rebuild needed to confirm.
Natural language format worse than terse. Grep went 0.375→0.125, git 0.357→0.214. Original "tool_name: N calls" format was better. Revert.
Shell descriptions + grep patterns add noise; 0.2812→0.2619. Terse format still best for embeddings. Pausing to add FTS5 comparison to benchmark.
Three-mode comparison added. FTS5=0.3509 > hybrid=0.3122 > semantic=0.2619. FTS5 blind spot: 'writing new files'=0.000 (no stemming). Hybrid hit@10=1.0.
Porter stemmer + tool descriptions in FTS5 index. fts5_recall: 0.3509→0.4246 (+21%). 'writing new files' fixed (0→0.300). hit@10=1.0. FTS5 now clearly best for tool-usage queries.
AND→OR priority FTS5 query logic. fts5: 0.4246→0.4461. 'writing new files' 0.300→0.450. Still stuck at 0.571 for git (AND fallback may not be helping there).
Per-conv aggregation: writing+errors improved but grep/edit/git worse. Net: 0.4461→0.4322. Per-call documents better for BM25 precision. Revert.
Rarest-keyword anchor: errors/writing improved but editing/git/grep hurt. Net worse than simple AND→OR priority. Revert.
Rarest-keyword-only fallback still worse than AND→OR priority. Errors 0.310→0.276, edit 0.476→0.381. AND→OR (0.4461) remains best. Revert.
